title: Growing autonomy
description: Replace recurring purchases with local supplies, then recover useful outputs. Keep enough labor and reserves for losses.
tip: Start with water and food reliability. Add reuse and renewable supplies before expanding demand.
boundary: Seeds and tree starts still need outside supplies. Biogas can fuel cooking.

title: System overview
description: Land, labor, supplies and utilities constrain every village activity.
diagram:
flowchart TB
 Player[Player plans and policies] --> Work[Resident work and dispatch]
 Land[Land and access] --> Work
 Needs[Needs and social behavior] --> Work
 Work --> Build[Construction and maintenance]
 Work --> Production[Recipes and crafting]
 Work --> Farms[Cultivation and biology]
 Work --> Trade[Purchases and sales]
 Build --> Utilities[Water, sanitation and power]
 Production --> Goods[Physical inventories and hauling]
 Farms --> Goods
 Trade --> Goods
 Trade --> Money[Cash and commitments]
 Utilities --> Services[Services and productive conditions]
tip: Find the missing input before expanding. A local supply must cover use, losses and replacement.

title: Time, seasons and play modes
description: Use the clock to pause or change speed. A running village catches up when you return to its open tab. Pause to stop catch-up at the current moment. When everyone is asleep or away, time can advance at 64×. If this computer cannot hold the selected speed, the speed button shows the rate the village is really running at.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Mode{Play mode} -->|Story| Story[Finite supplies and biological waiting]
 Mode -->|Sandbox| Sandbox[Replenished supplies and no biological waiting]
 Clock[Clock controls] --> Running{Time running?}
 Running -->|Yes| Calendar[Days, seasons and schedules advance]
 Running -->|No| Hold[Village activity pauses]
 Clock --> Skip{Advance days}
 Skip -->|Normal steps| Calendar
 Skip -->|Fast simulation| Coarse[Larger steps: decisions and totals can differ]
 Coarse --> Calendar
 Calendar --> Weather[Seasonal rain, cloud cover and temperature]
 Weather --> Effects[Water recharge, crop stress and hydration demand]
 Calendar --> Residents[Resident needs, trips and work]
boundary: Sandbox also skips asset upkeep and tool wear.
tip: Advance days runs the same simulation steps while you wait. Fast simulation takes larger steps, so resident decisions and resource totals can differ from normal play. Check upcoming milestones first; supplies, bills, weather and resident needs continue. Stop here keeps progress and pauses the village. When the days end, a recap lists what changed in savings, food, water and building work.

title: World, terrain and navigation
description: Terrain and access determine where buildings fit and residents can work.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Setup[Seed, biome and resource settings] --> World[Terrain, river and natural sites]
 World --> Grid[Map cells and elevation]
 Edit[Terrain edits and foundations] --> Grid
 Grid --> Check{Footprint and access valid?}
 Plan[Building or field footprint] --> Check
 Check -->|No| Reject[Explain placement constraint]
 Check -->|Yes| Place[Place project]
 Place --> Routes[Recheck walking routes]
 Grid --> Routes
 Routes --> Reach{Reachable work or service point?}
 Reach -->|Yes| Walk[Resident walks to target]
 Reach -->|No| Block[Wait or choose another action]
boundary: Terrain editing currently has no labor or cash cost.
tip: Keep stores, work sites and water routes close. Building placement and relocation check whether residents would lose access to food or drinking water.

title: Resident needs, rest and homes
description: Residents eat around breakfast, lunch and dinner, and sleep through the night. Urgent needs can interrupt work.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Time[Time, activity and personality] --> Decay[Needs and energy change]
 Decay --> Urgent{Need break, meal time or scheduled sleep?}
 Urgent -->|No| Available[Available for work or downtime]
 Urgent -->|Yes| Interrupt[Suspend or defer work safely]
 Interrupt --> Target{Suitable reachable service or rest place?}
 Target -->|Yes| Travel[Walk to service or assigned / available home]
 Target -->|No| Fallback[Try fallback or expose blocked need]
 Travel --> Consume[Consume food, water or service capacity as applicable]
 Consume --> Recover[Restore need or energy]
 Recover --> Resume[Reconsider unfinished work]
 Fallback --> Resume
 Resume --> Urgent
 Heat[Heat and active work] --> Thirst[Individual hydration demand]
 Thirst --> Target
 Fresh[Potable water and travel bottles] --> Consume
tip: Keep food, potable water and homes reachable. Residents seek drinks before thirst becomes urgent and normally sleep 7.5–9 hours; urgent bathroom breaks resume the same night’s rest.

title: Personality, relationships and downtime
description: Preferences influence work, leisure and willing conversations.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Profile[Resident identity and preferences] --> Choice[Choose leisure, work preference or thought]
 State[Needs, commitments and time of day] --> Choice
 Choice --> Social{Conversation wanted and partner willing?}
 Social -->|Yes| Meet[Both residents reach meeting place]
 Meet --> Talk[Conversation]
 Talk --> Relationship[Friendship and recent memories]
 Social -->|No| Personal[Read, stretch, sit or stroll]
 Personal --> Memory[Personal-time memory]
 Hope[Completed personal building hope] --> Memory
 Relationship --> Choice
 Memory --> Choice
 Work[New work or urgent need] --> Interrupt[Interrupt casual downtime]
boundary: Residents do not autonomously place buildings.
tip: Leave time and reachable places for social contact and recreation.

title: Work dispatch and interruption
description: Available residents choose work using needs, assignments and priorities.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Resident[Resident chooses an action] --> Committed{Committed to trip, sleep or need?}
 Committed -->|Yes| Continue[Advance committed action]
 Committed -->|No| Existing{Unfinished assigned operation?}
 Existing -->|Yes| Resume[Try to resume work]
 Existing -->|No| Select[Evaluate services, upkeep and work priorities]
 Resume --> Gate{Inputs, tools, access and capacity available?}
 Select --> Gate
 Gate -->|Yes| Do[Travel, carry or work]
 Gate -->|No| Explain[Record blocker and consider alternatives]
 Do --> Needs[Re-evaluate needs and cargo safety]
 Explain --> Idle[Other work or finite downtime]
 Needs --> Resident
boundary: Available residents take farm and animal work before starting lower-priority jobs. Needs, rest and deliveries already in progress still take precedence.
tip: Protect essential work first. A large queue cannot replace available workers.

title: Construction and material staging
description: Residents carry committed materials and assemble buildings.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Blueprint[Choose valid blueprint and rotation] --> Bill[Capture material bill and work requirement]
 Bill --> Stock{Required supplies available?}
 Stock -->|No| Purchase[Purchase or produce missing supplies]
 Purchase --> Stock
 Stock -->|Yes| Reserve[Commit materials to project]
 Reserve --> Haul[Residents carry loads via stores or depot]
 Haul --> Stage[Materials staged at site]
 Stage --> Assemble[Accessible crew performs assembly]
 Assemble --> More{Materials or work remaining?}
 More -->|Yes| Haul
 More -->|No| Complete[Completed building joins available services]
 Needs[Needs and equipment] --> Assemble
boundary: Money pays for supplies and transport; resident construction labor is not a wage charge.
tip: Build only what your stores and carrying capacity can support. A planned site is marked on the ground with an outline, corner stakes and a faint shape of the building until work begins.

title: Relocation, demolition and salvage
description: Moving or removing a building requires access, resident work and eligibility.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Request[Request move, salvage or demolition] --> Validate{Eligible and no conflicting work?}
 Validate -->|No| Block[Explain blocker]
 Validate -->|Yes| Vacate[Wait for occupants to leave]
 Vacate --> Work[Resident reaches site and performs work]
 Work --> Mode{Operation}
 Mode -->|Move| Check[Revalidate destination and relocate]
 Mode -->|Remove| Capacity{Space for recoverable materials?}
 Capacity -->|No| Wait[Wait for storage space]
 Capacity -->|Yes| Return[Return recovery fraction to stores]
 Return --> Cleanup[Remove utility links and clear assignments]
 Cleanup --> Loss[Record material and stored utility losses]
 Check --> Routes[Refresh navigation]
boundary: Salvage is not a full refund.
tip: Salvage usable materials before replacing a building. Recovery is partial.

title: Production and output hauling
description: Inputs travel to work sites. Finished output travels back to storage.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Queue[Queue recipe or bed job] --> Validate{Site, input and job constraints pass?}
 Validate -->|No| Block[Explain missing condition]
 Validate -->|Yes| Pickup[Acquire inputs from stores]
 Pickup --> Travel[Carry inputs to reachable work position]
 Travel --> Biology{Biological waiting required?}
 Biology -->|Yes| Grow[Release worker while biology advances]
 Grow --> Process[Resident processing or collection work]
 Biology -->|No| Process
 Process --> Resolve[Finished crop or recipe output]
 Resolve --> Loads[Split output into physical loads]
 Loads --> Carry[Carry to available storage]
 Carry --> Remaining{Output remaining?}
 Remaining -->|Yes| Loads
 Remaining -->|No| Done[Mark operation complete]
 Target[Repeat target and protected reserves] --> Queue
boundary: Planting beds, perennial crops and recipes have different waiting and harvest rules.
tip: Residents start work at nearby sites themselves when stores fall below two batches and inputs and storage are ready. Queue work yourself for distant sites, tree felling and installations; your orders come first. Use Food Almanac policies to manage kitchen reserves.

title: Crafting and learned skills
description: Crafting requires compatible materials, tools, workstations and skill.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Recipe[Choose craft or repair recipe] --> Site{Compatible workstation?}
 Site -->|No| Block[Explain requirement]
 Site -->|Yes| Skill{Resident has required skill level?}
 Skill -->|No| Block
 Skill -->|Yes| Tools{Required tools usable and available?}
 Tools -->|No| Block
 Tools -->|Yes| Stages[Perform craft stages with materials]
 Stages --> Practice[Accumulate skill practice]
 Practice --> Rate[Skill affects work multiplier]
 Rate --> Stages
 Stages --> Complete[Deliver crafted item or finish repair]
boundary: Some recipes require a minimum skill level.
tip: Choose recipes your residents can perform with available tools and skills.

title: Shared tools, wear and repair
description: Shared tools improve work. Use causes wear; repair consumes supplies.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Task[Resident task] --> Tool{Usable tool available?}
 Tool -->|Yes| Loan[Reserve tool for resident and task]
 Loan --> Work[Apply equipment work benefit]
 Work --> Wear[Accumulate active-use wear]
 Wear --> Broken{Unit worn out?}
 Broken -->|Yes| Return[Release loan and continue basic work where allowed]
 Broken -->|No| Work
 Tool -->|No| Base[Basic work or hard craft blocker]
 Return --> Repair[Repair recipe consumes supplies and work]
 Repair --> Tool
 Break[Need, rest or task completion] --> Release[Release shared loan]
boundary: Some crafting tools are mandatory; other equipment is a speed benefit.
tip: Share tools and retain repair supplies. Metal parts still depend on town.

title: Natural gathering and extraction
description: Gathering sites are either finite or recover over time.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Site[Generated patch, tree or deposit] --> Ready{Accessible and available?}
 Ready -->|No| Reason[Depleted, recovering or inaccessible]
 Ready -->|Yes| Gather[Resident gathers, cuts or extracts]
 Gather --> Output[Carry gathered output to stores]
 Output --> Kind{Resource behavior}
 Kind -->|Finite| Deplete[Advance extraction or felling state]
 Kind -->|Renewable patch| Cooldown[Set next ready time]
 Cooldown --> Ready
 Deplete --> Left{Capacity remains?}
 Left -->|Yes| Ready
 Left -->|No| Exhausted[No further extraction]
boundary: Wild fruit, bamboo and forage take time to recover after gathering. A site nobody can reach on foot is left alone and checked again each day.
tip: Rotate renewable gathering sites. Finite deposits will eventually run out.

title: Field and greenhouse cultivation
description: Manage a whole planting area or inspect one bed. Each bed keeps its own crop, care and harvest cycle.
boundary: Harvest quantities resolve once. Delayed harvest can reduce yield; clearing returns residues only. Fields snap to 2 m map cells.
tip: Residents prepare beds, plant the selected crop with stored seeds, and harvest ripe beds automatically. With Auto-buy on, residents order missing seeds or cuttings when shared savings can cover them and collection; each field, garden and greenhouse has its own Auto-buy seeds & compost switch, which also covers compost for Apply compost work. Keep water, work access and storage available.

title: Soil, water stress and residue cycles
description: Water, fertility, cover and accumulated stress determine crop development.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Rain[Outdoor rain] --> Moisture[Soil moisture]
 Supply[Withdrawn irrigation water] --> Moisture
 Cover[Residue surface cover] --> Evap[Reduced evaporation demand]
 Evap --> Moisture
 Moisture --> Conditions[Growth conditions and accumulated stress]
 Fertility[Available fertility] --> Conditions
 Density[Plant density and competition] --> Conditions
 Season[Outdoor season factor] --> Conditions
 Conditions --> Biomass[Growth and standing biomass]
 Biomass --> Harvest[Harvest or clearing]
 Harvest --> Export[Crop output removes fertility]
 Harvest --> Residue[Recoverable residues]
 Residue --> Cover
 Residue --> Collect[Collect once for compost ingredients]
 Compost[Applied compost] --> Decay[Decomposition over time]
 Residue --> Decay
 Decay --> Fertility
 Decay --> Organic[Retained organic matter]
 Decay --> Gas[Accounted decomposition losses]
 Conditions --> Damage[Cumulative drought damage]
 Damage --> Failure[Failed crop: clear and replant]
boundary: Late watering cannot erase drought damage. Failed or expired crops must be cleared.
tip: Leave cover or compost collected residues. Both return material with losses; neither guarantees soil balance. Cassava, sweet potato and cowpeas survive dry soil longer than the other crops and keep growing through the dry season.

title: Perennial and other biological cycles
description: Trees, perennial crops and compost develop while residents do other work.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Inputs[Recipe inputs and initial resident work] --> Wait[Biology continues without a worker]
 First[First orchard establishment delay] --> Wait
 Factors[Recipe-specific season, moisture and fertility] --> Wait
 Wait --> Ready[Ready for resident collection or processing]
 Ready --> Delay[Delay after maturity]
 Delay --> Loss[Perishable output may decline]
 Ready --> Work[Resident collection work]
 Health[Animal health where applicable] --> Yield[Available output]
 Work --> Yield
 Loss --> Yield
 Yield --> Store[Physical hauling to storage]
 Store --> Repeat[Repeat if resources and policy allow]
tip: Managed timber needs six favorable growing years, longer in dry or cool conditions. Each later rotation consumes four replacement seedlings; residents plant, fell and haul raw logs for processing. An orchard grows the fruit tree of its land: pequi in the Cerrado and umbu in the Caatinga need far less irrigation and sit out dry spells. A coffee grove gives its first crop in the third year and one a year after that; dried coffee keeps and sells to the town café.

title: Livestock care and animal products
description: Animal care consumes fodder, water and labor. Health affects supported products.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Animals[Stocked animals] --> Demand[Feed and drinking-water demand]
 Care[Resident care job] --> Reserves[Finite on-site feed and water]
 Reserves --> Demand
 Demand --> Adequate{Enough reserves?}
 Adequate -->|Yes| Health[Health and product accumulation]
 Adequate -->|No| Harm[Health declines; production drops]
 Health --> Collect[Resident collects stored product]
 Collect --> Haul[Haul eggs or milk to stores]
boundary: Animals consume feed and water over time. Refill their supplies separately from collecting products.
tip: Residents tend stocked animals and collect available eggs and milk even when the pantry is full. If fodder runs short, they gather it from available wild forage. Keep drinking water and a clear path to the animals.

title: Water supply and irrigation
description: Collect or pump water, store it, and purify drinking water.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 River[River] --> Carry[Resident collection and hauling]
 River --> Pump[Powered pump]
 Ground[Groundwater well] --> Pump
 Rain[Rain collection] --> Untreated[Untreated water storage]
 Carry --> Untreated
 Pump --> Untreated
 Untreated --> Purify[Manual purification or powered filtering]
 Purify --> Fresh[Fresh water]
 Fresh --> Needs[Drinking and hygiene]
 Untreated --> Irrigate[Crop irrigation withdrawal]
 Fresh --> Irrigate
 Links[Completed compatible water links] --> Transfer[Capacity-limited transfers]
 Fresh --> Transfer
 Untreated --> Transfer
 Transfer --> Users[Connected storage and services]
 Capacity[Storage capacity and source exhaustion] --> Block[Transfer or task waits]
 Weather[Seasonal rainfall] --> Recharge[Shared watershed recharge]
 Recharge --> River
 Recharge --> Ground
 Pump --> Drawdown[Shared source withdrawal]
 Carry --> Drawdown
 Drawdown --> Capacity
boundary: A river connection alone is not an automatic pump.
tip: Watch source reserves through the dry season. A dry world is a drought year with fewer rainy days, and Caatinga land returns little of its rain to rivers and wells. Rain recharges the watershed; pumps and manual collection draw from the same finite supply.

title: Sanitation and wastewater treatment
description: Waste treatment frees capacity and can recover irrigation water.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Hygiene[Washing and hygiene] --> Grey[Greywater]
 Toilet[Toilet use] --> Sewage[Sewage / sealed waste]
 Grey --> Wetland[Wetland treatment]
 Wetland --> Reuse[85 percent to irrigation water]
 Wetland --> Loss[15 percent accounted loss]
 Sewage --> Banana[Banana treatment]
 Sewage --> Digester[Biodigester]
 Banana --> Removed[Accounted water removal]
 Digester --> Removed
 Digester --> Gas[Biogas counter]
 Sewage --> Service[Resident sanitation service]
 Full[Full or inaccessible service] --> Block[Blocked use or servicing need]
 Gas --> Cooking[Kitchen fallback when electricity is unavailable]
boundary: The biogas balance can fuel kitchen work; it is not a bounded gas network or electricity generator.
tip: Keep waste capacity available. Wetlands recover irrigation water, not drinking water.

title: Power generation, storage and loads
description: Local generation and batteries serve connected loads; grid backup covers affordable shortages.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Sources[Solar, hydro and optional home solar] --> Energy[Generated energy plus battery storage]
 Demand[Active machinery, pumps, cooling and night lighting] --> Allocate[Allocate by load priority]
 Energy --> Allocate
 Allocate --> Short{Shortfall with grid connection and affordable cash?}
 Short -->|Yes| Grid[Buy capped grid energy for loads]
 Short -->|No| Unpowered[Unsupplied loads remain off]
 Grid --> Powered[Supplied services run]
 Allocate --> Powered
 Energy --> Excess[Surplus local generation]
 Excess --> Battery[Charge with 90 percent efficiency]
 Battery --> Energy
 Excess --> Curtail[Account for excess beyond capacity]
 Powered --> Visual[Window emission and nearby light spill]
boundary: Grid backup does not charge batteries.
tip: Match generation and batteries to actual demand before disconnecting the grid. Replacement equipment remains imported.

title: Food batches, cooking and spoilage
description: Food keeps its identity and age during storage, processing and transport.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Crop[Named harvested crop or purchased food] --> Lots[Inventory with expiry-bearing lots]
 Lots --> Cook[Explicit ingredient recipe and resident work]
 Cook --> Meals[Prepared meal lots]
 Lots --> Preserve[Preservation recipe]
 Preserve --> Long[Longer-lived food lots]
 Power[Powered refrigeration] --> Slow[Slow ageing of eligible stored food]
 Slow --> Lots
 Lots --> Expired{Expired?}
 Meals --> Expired
 Long --> Expired
 Expired -->|Yes| Waste[Remove spoiled food and account organic waste]
 Expired -->|No| Use[Eating, recipe input or trade]
 Use --> Transit[Preserve batch age in cargo and reservations]
 Lots --> Forecast[Expiry-aware pantry forecast]
 Forecast --> Policy[Optional fresh-meal and provision policies]
 Policy --> Cook
boundary: Refrigeration capacity is measured in liters. Uncooked crops do not count as ready portions.
tip: Use the Food Almanac to inspect expiry, fresh meals, dried provisions and refrigeration. Automatic kitchens can cook harvested crops even when the pantry is empty. Cassava can also be toasted into farinha provisions, which keep 30 days against 10 for other dried provisions. With automatic food management on, residents sell food that would spoil before the village could eat it. Recipes that consume ready-to-eat food protect a one-day reserve.

title: Inventory ownership and material accounting
description: Goods can be in stores, committed, carried, processed or installed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Stores[Available stores] --> Reserve[Construction / recipe / export commitments]
 Reserve --> Cargo[Resident or vehicle cargo]
 Cargo --> Site[Staged site inputs]
 Site --> Process[Construction or processing]
 Process --> Output[Resolved output awaiting delivery]
 Output --> Stores
 Process --> Loss[Recorded conversion losses and consumption]
 Sources[Purchases and environmental / biological inputs] --> Stores
 Stores --> Ledger[Material movements and ownership]
 Cargo --> Ledger
 Site --> Ledger
 Output --> Ledger
 Units[Item-specific mass and volume] --> Capacity[Cargo and displayed physical quantities]
boundary: Ledger entries explain movement; they are not a second stockpile.
tip: Check goods already reserved or in transit before buying more. A manifest is not extra stock. Organic residues sit in a heap outdoors and take no storage room; a compost station turns them into compost.

title: Purchases, sales and physical transport
description: Purchases and sales need supply, demand, capacity and physical transport.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Request[Purchase request or sale policy] --> Quote[Supplier stock or buyer quote and demand]
 Quote --> Reserve[Reserve goods, cash commitments or exports]
 Reserve --> Method{Transport method}
 Method -->|Resident pickup| Car[Available driver and car; town operating hours]
 Method -->|Paid supplier| Freight[Reserve delivery cost and capacity]
 Method -->|Project order over one car load| Freight
 Car --> Cargo[Load within mass and volume limits]
 Cargo --> Town[Travel to town and settle eligible sales once]
 Town --> Return[Return with purchased goods or unsold lots]
 Return --> Unload[Unload into stores or project shipment]
 Freight --> Unload
 Consolidate[Trip consolidation and protected reserves] --> Car
 Age[Perishable lot ageing in transit] --> Return
boundary: There are two resident vehicles plus paid freight. A project order too large for one car load arrives by supplier truck even when purchases are set to resident pickup. Truck goods count as received once the truck has parked and unloaded.
tip: Set the food reserve and daily food budget in Resources. Plan for three portions per resident per day. Emergency purchases count incoming food and include transport in the daily budget. Check dedicated-trip fuel costs or hold a sale for a shared pickup. Manual sales can draw on household reserves.

title: Cash, commitments and forecasts
description: Income and expenses change cash; commitments reduce what can be spent.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Income[Settled sales and outside-job income] --> Cash[Shared money balance]
 Costs[Supplies, transport and grid purchases] --> Cash
 Cash --> Budget[Subtract commitments and policy reserves]
 Budget --> Decision{New expense affordable?}
 Decision -->|Yes| Spend[Perform transaction]
 Decision -->|No| Wait[Wait or explain shortage]
 Spend --> History[Categorized money history]
 Income --> History
 History --> Days[Aggregate completed calendar days]
 Days --> Forecast[Observed operating forecast]
 Forecast --> UI[Finance inspection]
boundary: The forecast is an estimate from observed activity, not a guaranteed future economy.
tip: Keep a cash reserve for unavoidable imports, maintenance and transport.

title: Optional outside employment
description: In Story, book a resident for one eight-hour shift from Finances or Residents. Their profile also offers recurring four-hour weekday shifts.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Once[Book one eight-hour shift] --> Bus[Catch the morning bus when rested and free]
 Repeat[Enable four-hour weekday shifts] --> Bus
 Bus --> Work[Work in town]
 Work --> Home[Return to camp and collect wages]
boundary: Residents take at most one shift per day. A day booking takes priority over a recurring shift. The employer covers the bus fare upfront when village cash is short and deducts it on payday.
tip: Check the take-home pay before booking. Leave someone in camp if you need building materials collected or a house finished that day.

title: Neighbours: mutirões, courses and festas
description: Open Neighbours (O) to call a mutirão, offer a weekend course or hold a festa. The neighbours' goodwill decides how many people come.
diagram:
flowchart LR
 Goodwill[Neighbours' goodwill] --> Turnout[How many people come]
 Turnout --> Mutirao[Mutirão: neighbours work on one building]
 Turnout --> Course[Weekend course: a friend teaches paying visitors]
 Turnout --> Festa[Festa: friends and neighbours gather]
 Meals[Prepared meals in stores] --> Mutirao
 Meals --> Course
 Meals --> Festa
 Mutirao --> Owed[The village owes one day of work]
 Owed --> Return[A friend spends a day on a neighbour's land]
 Return --> Goodwill
 Festa --> Goodwill
 Course --> Fees[Fees into village savings]
 Roda[Sunday roda at a gathering place] --> Minutes[What the friends said is kept]
boundary: Neighbours work only on a building whose materials are all on site, and leave the last touches to the friends. A mutirão or course happens on a Saturday or Sunday. The region fills one course a fortnight. Neighbours are not residents: they arrive for the event and leave after it.
tip: Cook before you invite. Neighbours without lunch go home, and people sent home hungry think less of the village. Return the day of work you owe before you ask for help again.

title: Asset maintenance and replacement
description: Age and use reduce condition. Service needs parts, access and labor. Cars also weather where they are parked; a car shelter slows that to a third.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Use[Time, active assets and vehicle distance] --> Condition[Condition and age change]
 Parked[Cars parked in the open: sun and rain] --> Condition
 Shelter[Car shelter over the parking clearing] -->|Weathering three times slower| Parked
 Condition --> Due{Service or replacement due?}
 Due -->|Yes| Queue[Queue maintenance job]
 Queue --> Gate{Parts, allowance and accessible site?}
 Gate -->|No| Wait[Expose missing parts, budget or access]
 Gate -->|Yes| Work[Resident collects supplies and services asset]
 Work --> Restore[Restore condition or reset replacement age]
 Restore --> Condition
 Condition --> Capacity[Service factor and battery capacity affect utilities]
 Due -->|No| Continue[Continue operation]
tip: In Finances, set a daily feed and repair shopping budget to cover missing supplies and transport. Zero disables shopping. Residents still need to receive the goods and do the work.

title: Inspecting village conditions
description: Use the village counters, map lenses and Almanac to spot shortages and decide what needs attention.
diagram:
flowchart TD
 Village[Current village conditions] --> Counters[Food, battery, and Water & sanitation counters]
 Village --> Lenses[Map lenses show conditions by location]
 Village --> Almanac[Almanac shows supplies and work policies]
 Counters --> Details[Hover for details or click to manage]
 Lenses --> Inspect[Select a bed or building for details]
 Almanac --> Policies[Adjust policies for village work]
tip: Check food, water and battery status before adding demand. Open Water & sanitation for toilet and washing conditions.
